import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import SeqDiagram from '../../../../components/SeqDiagram.astro';

**Task:** do something in your app without a client asking each time (sweep
expired bookings every minute, refresh data every hour), and do work a call
cannot (several HTTP requests, seconds of waiting) without holding up the log.

- A **timer** (`#[app::every]`) is a logged write the node runs on an interval,
  as the system caller.
- An **action** (`#[app::action]`) runs outside the log on the app's leader.
  It has no state of its own: it reads with views, writes with calls and talks
  to the outside world with HTTP.

The example is a watchlist of company domains: `watch` adds one and looks it
up at once, an hourly timer looks every domain up again, and the `enrich`
action asks an outside service for the industry and stores it. It builds and
its harness test below passes against the SDK in this repository; the patterns
come from `apps/v2-fixtures/kv` (`beat`, `startEnrich`, `enrich`) and
`apps/rooms` (`releaseNoShows`).

## The app

```rust
use calimero_sdk::prelude::*;
use calimero_sdk::Request;

#[app::state(version = 1)]
pub struct Watchlist {
    /// The domains watched; the value is the slot of the tick that last queued it.
    domains: UnorderedMap<String, u64>,
    /// What `enrich` brought back, by domain.
    industries: UnorderedMap<String, String>,
    /// What `onActionFailed` was told, by action id: `"<method>|<reason>"`.
    failures: UnorderedMap<String, String>,
}

#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
struct DomainArg<'a> {
    domain: &'a str,
}

#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
struct Industry<'a> {
    domain: &'a str,
    industry: &'a str,
}

#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct Answer {
    industry: String,
}

#[app::error]
pub enum Error {
    NotATick,
}

/// Domains one tick queues: one run may start at most 100 actions.
const PER_TICK: u32 = 50;

#[app::logic]
impl Watchlist {
    #[app::init]
    pub fn init() -> app::Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self::load())
    }

    /// Watch `domain` and look it up now; answers the action's key.
    pub fn watch(&mut self, domain: String) -> app::Result<String> {
        self.domains.insert(&domain, &0)?;
        env::start_action("enrich", &DomainArg { domain: &domain })
    }

    /// Every hour, look the watched domains up again.
    #[app::every("1h")]
    pub fn refresh(&mut self) -> app::Result<()> {
        let Some(tick) = env::timer() else {
            app::bail!(Error::NotATick);
        };
        let page = self.domains.page(FindOpts::default().limit(PER_TICK))?;
        for (domain, _) in page.items {
            env::start_action("enrich", &DomainArg { domain: &domain })?;
            self.domains.insert(&domain, &tick.scheduled)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Runs on the leader, outside the log: reads with a view, fetches, writes with a call.
    #[app::action]
    pub fn enrich(ctx: &mut ActionCtx, domain: String) -> app::Result<()> {
        let known: Option<String> = ctx.view("industry", &DomainArg { domain: &domain })?;
        let request = Request::get(format!("https://enrich.example.com/v1/{domain}"))
            .header("Idempotency-Key", &ctx.key())
            .header("Authorization", "Bearer {{secret:ENRICH_KEY}}");
        let answer: Answer = ctx.fetch(&request)?.json()?;
        if known.as_deref() != Some(answer.industry.as_str()) {
            ctx.call::<(), _>(
                "applyIndustry",
                &Industry {
                    domain: &domain,
                    industry: &answer.industry,
                },
            )?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Only the app's own actions write here.
    #[app::allow(action)]
    pub fn apply_industry(&mut self, domain: String, industry: String) -> app::Result<()> {
        self.industries.insert(&domain, &industry)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The node runs this as the action's starter when an action fails for good.
    pub fn on_action_failed(
        &mut self,
        action_id: String,
        method: String,
        reason: String,
    ) -> app::Result<()> {
        self.failures
            .insert(&action_id, &format!("{method}|{reason}"))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    #[app::view]
    pub fn industry(&self, domain: String) -> app::Result<Option<String>> {
        Ok(self.industries.get(&domain)?)
    }
}
```

## Timers

```rust
#[app::every("1h")]
pub fn refresh(&mut self) -> app::Result<()> { /* ... */ }
```

- The interval is `"<n>s"`, `"<n>m"` or `"<n>h"` with `n > 0`.
  Anything else is a compile error.
- A timer takes `&mut self` and no arguments, and its caller is always
  `System`.
  `every` implies `#[app::allow(system)]`, so the ABI says `allowSystem: true`;
  `apps/rooms` writes both, which changes nothing.
- No client can call a timer: `/intents` and `/views` refuse it with the app
  error `WrongKind`.
- Inside it, `env::timer()` is `Some(TimerInfo { scheduled, previous })`: the
  slot this tick is for and the slot applied before it (`None` on the timer's
  first tick), both app times in milliseconds.
  It is `None` in every other kind of run.
  `env::time_now()` is the time of the tick's log entry, a little after
  `scheduled`.

### When ticks run

Slots are counted from the moment the app was installed: the first is one
interval after it, then one every interval.
The app's leader looks for due slots every 100 ms (`TIMER_POLL`) and proposes
each tick as an ordinary log entry, so followers apply its diff and never run
it themselves.

- **Missed slots are not replayed.**
  After a gap (no leader, a long tick, a restart) the leader runs only the
  latest due slot, once; `previous` tells the method how far back the last
  applied one is.
- **A tick is applied once.**
  A slot at or before the applied one changes nothing, so a new leader does
  not repeat a tick.
- **A failed tick still counts.**
  An app error or a trap is logged as that slot's outcome, its writes thrown
  away, and the next tick is the next slot.
  Only a tick that hit its time budget, or ran while the node could not serve
  its data, is not logged; the leader proposes the same slot again on its next
  poll.
- A tick runs with a call's budget (2 s of wall clock, the same fuel and
  memory) and a call's write limits (1 MiB per entry, 10,000 writes), so keep
  each tick's work bounded, as `PER_TICK` does here and `MAX_RELEASES_PER_TICK`
  does in `apps/rooms`.
- A timer may write, emit events, send cross-app calls, make outbound
  requests (`env::fetch`, recorded in the tick's entry; [Call an external service](/build/guides/outbound/)),
  start compute runs ([Compute actions](/build/guides/compute-actions/)) and
  start actions.

The tick key is `tick:<method>:<slot>`, so a synchronous cross-app call a tick
makes replays if the tick is re-run.

## Actions

```rust
#[app::action]
pub fn enrich(ctx: &mut ActionCtx, domain: String) -> app::Result<()> { /* ... */ }
```

An action takes no `self`; its first parameter is `ctx: &mut ActionCtx`, and
the rest are its arguments, decoded from JSON like any method's.
It cannot carry `confirm`, `public` or `allow(action)`.

### Start one

Three ways, each logged as a start in an entry, so an action is never lost to
a leader change:

- **From a call or a timer:** `env::start_action("enrich", &args)` returns the
  action's key, `a.<term>.<seq>.<n>`.
  The start is kept only if the run succeeds: a call that fails starts nothing.
  A run may start at most 100 actions (`StartAction` error past that).
- **From a client:** calling the action method itself through `/intents`
  (`client.apps.call` in mero-js) logs the start and answers
  `{ "actionId": "a.…" }` as the result.
  An account or an API key may start one, as the app's access allows.
- **From a test:** see [below](#test-it).

An app keeps at most 1,000 pending actions (`MAX_PENDING_ACTIONS`); one started
past that fails at once.

### What it can do

| `ctx.` | Does | Fails with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key()` | The action's key, the same on every attempt. Send it as the remote side's idempotency key. | |
| `view::<T, _>(method, &args)` | Runs a view of this app on the leader's current state and decodes its JSON result. | `ActionView { message }`, or `BadOutput` |
| `call::<T, _>(method, &args)` | Runs a method of this app as one logged call, as the action's starter. | `ActionCall { message }` (the method's own error included), or `BadOutput` |
| `fetch(&Request)` | One HTTPS request over `wasi:http`, through the outbound gate; the response is read whole. | `Fetch { message }` |

- Methods are named as the ABI names them: `applyIndustry`, not
  `apply_industry`.
- An action has **no storage**: every read is a `view`, every write a `call`.
  Each call is its own log entry.
- `#[app::allow(action)]` on a method makes it reachable only from the app's
  own actions: a client that calls `applyIndustry` gets the app error
  `Forbidden`.
  Use it for the method an action writes its result through, so no client can
  forge one.
- `fetch` reaches only a URL under a prefix the signed release's manifest
  declares under `outbound`, approved by the organization (or, per governance,
  the operator) and allowed by the operator.
  `{{secret:NAME}}` in a header or the body is filled in by the node and
  redacted from the response.
  Declaring and approving prefixes, and setting secrets, are in
  [Call an external service](/build/guides/outbound/).
  `Request::get(url)`, `Request::post(url, body)` and `.header(name, value)`
  build a request; `Response` has `status`, `headers`, `body`, `json()` and
  `text()`.

### Retries and failure

An action is **at least once**: only the leader runs it, and a new leader
resumes every action that has not ended, with the same key.

- A run that times out is retried with backoff (1 s, doubling), up to 5
  attempts in all.
- An app error, a trap or out-of-fuel ends it at once, as failed.
  So does a method the app's current release no longer has.
- A retried action's `ctx.call`s replay instead of applying twice: each call's
  log key is derived from the action's key, the method, a hash of the
  arguments and how many identical calls came before it in the run.
  Your outbound requests are not replayed, so send `ctx.key()` as the remote
  side's idempotency key, as `enrich` does.

When an action fails for good, the node does two things for its starter:

1. sends them an `ActionFailed { actionId, method, reason }` event (audience:
   that account), which a client following the app's [events](/build/guides/events/)
   receives;
2. runs the app's `onActionFailed(actionId, method, reason)`, if it has a call
   method of that name, as the starter (so it must accept that caller).
   The reason is at most 512 bytes.

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Timer interval | `<n>s`, `<n>m` or `<n>h`, `n > 0` |
| A tick's budget | 2 s wall clock, a call's fuel and memory |
| An action run's budget | 10 s wall clock, a call's fuel and memory |
| Attempts per action | 5 (timeouts only) |
| Actions one run may start | 100 |
| Pending actions per app | 1,000 |
| Actions one node runs at once, across its apps | 8 |
| `ctx.call`s per action run | 1,000 |
| HTTP requests per run (action, call or tick) | 8, request bodies up to 1 MiB (`MAX_HTTP_REQUESTS`, `MAX_HTTP_BODY_BYTES`) |
| One response in a call or tick (`env::fetch`) | awaited at most 1.5 s, inside the 2 s budget |

The full table is in [Limits](/protocol/limits/), and the protocol in
[Actions](/protocol/execution/#actions-component-apps).

<Aside type="caution">
  The leader sees an outbound response before anything is logged, and
  attestation covers the code that made the request, not the remote server's
  answer. Store from an action only what you would trust that service for.
</Aside>

## Test it

The SDK's `TestApp` runs the real component. `t.tick(method)` runs a timer for
the slot at the harness clock, `t.advance(ms)` moves the clock,
`t.mock_http(host, handler)` answers an action's requests, and
`t.run_started_actions()` runs every action started so far, each as its
starter (`t.as_(a).action(method, args)` starts and runs one at once).
Retries, the replay of sub-call keys and the 10 s budget are the node's, not
the harness's.

```rust
use calimero_sdk::testing::{Failure, HttpResponse, Org, TestApp};
use serde_json::json;

#[test]
fn a_tick_queues_lookups_that_fill_the_watchlist() {
    let mut t = TestApp::new(component(), Org::new(), 1_700_000_000_000);
    t.mock_http("enrich.example.com", |_req| HttpResponse {
        status: 200,
        headers: Vec::new(),
        body: br#"{"industry":"retail"}"#.to_vec(),
    });
    let key = t
        .as_("owner")
        .call("watch", json!({ "domain": "acme.com" }))
        .unwrap();
    assert!(key.as_str().unwrap().starts_with("a."), "{key}");
    let ran = t.run_started_actions();
    assert!(ran.iter().all(Result::is_ok), "{ran:?}");
    assert_eq!(
        t.as_("owner")
            .view("industry", json!({ "domain": "acme.com" }))
            .unwrap(),
        json!("retail")
    );

    t.advance(3_600_000);
    t.tick("refresh").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(t.run_started_actions().len(), 1);

    let e = t
        .as_("owner")
        .call(
            "applyIndustry",
            json!({ "domain": "acme.com", "industry": "forged" }),
        )
        .unwrap_err();
    assert!(
        matches!(e, Failure::App { ref code, .. } if code == "Forbidden"),
        "{e:?}"
    );
}
```

`component()` builds the crate with `calimero_app_build::build_component`, as
`apps/v2-fixtures/kv/tests/harness.rs` does. On a cluster,
`actions_run_on_the_leader_and_reach_only_declared_approved_hosts`
(`crates/node/tests`) covers the outbound gate, secrets and redaction.

A scenario file ticks a timer with `{ "op": "tick", "method": "refresh" }` and
moves the clock with `advance`
([Testing](/build/testing/), [Testing strategy](/contribute/testing/#scenarios)).
